title: Streaming and background mode
summary: Streaming sends tokens as events so users see output early. Background mode runs a long call on the server while you poll. Batch handles bulk offline work.
useIf: A user waits on a response, a call outlasts an HTTP timeout, or you process large volumes offline.
avoidIf: You act on partial output. Never execute a tool call or parse JSON before the item is complete.

explain.md: **Streaming** returns server-sent events as the model generates. OpenAI Responses emits `response.created`, `response.in_progress`, `response.output_item.added`, `response.content_part.added`, repeated `response.output_text.delta`, then `response.output_text.done`, `response.content_part.done`, `response.output_item.done`, `response.completed`, and `error` on failure [[tr1]]. Anthropic sends `message_start`, then per block `content_block_start`, `content_block_delta` (`text_delta`, `input_json_delta`, `thinking_delta`) and `content_block_stop`, then `message_delta` with cumulative usage and `message_stop`. A `ping` can appear anywhere [[tr2]].

explain.title: Responses stream, in order
explain.alt: Events flow from response created through item added, content part added, repeated text deltas, text done, item done and response completed.
explain.src:
flowchart LR
  A[response.created] --> B[output_item.added]
  B --> C[content_part.added]
  C --> D[output_text.delta x many]
  D --> E[output_text.done]
  E --> F[output_item.done]
  F --> G[response.completed]

explain.md: Anthropic streams tool input one complete key and value at a time, so pauses are normal and you should not treat them as stalls. Buffer deltas and act when the item or block is done.

**Background mode** sets `background: true`. The call returns at once and you poll while the status is `queued` or `in_progress` [[r35]]. Under zero data retention a background response runs with `store=false` and its data sits on disk for roughly 10 minutes so you can poll, so fetch and persist the result promptly. Projects with Modified Abuse Monitoring keep a background response beyond polling only if `store=true` is set explicitly. On Azure, cancel is idempotent, you can resume a stream with `sequence_number`, and combining background with streaming has a known performance issue [[r34]].

explain.title: Pick by who is waiting
explain.md: A person watching: stream. A request that exceeds a timeout: background and poll. Nobody waiting: Batch at 50% of the Standard price with a 24 hour window, separate rate limits and no streaming on Anthropic batches [[r37]] [[r39]].

whereToUse: Chat and assistant UIs, to cut perceived latency with earlier first tokens
Voice and live captions, where partial text drives the next step
Deep research or long reasoning calls that run for minutes
Web apps behind gateways with short HTTP timeouts
Bulk nightly processing with Batch instead of per-request calls

use: Streaming when a person reads output as it appears
Background mode when a single call may outlast a timeout
Batch when results can wait up to 24 hours
avoid: Acting on partial tool arguments or partial JSON
Streaming where a downstream system needs only the final object
Background mode for bulk work that Batch can do at half price
flips: A ZDR project uses background mode: poll within the roughly 10 minute window and store the result yourself
Users disconnect often: use background with polling instead of one long stream
Streaming plus background on Azure shows slowdowns: poll without streaming

pitfalls.symptom: An email is sent with an incomplete address
pitfalls.cause: The app acted on tool arguments before the call finished streaming
pitfalls.fix: Execute tools only after the item is done and the arguments validate

pitfalls.symptom: A stream seems stalled during a tool call on Claude
pitfalls.cause: Tool input arrives one complete key and value at a time
pitfalls.fix: Wait for `content_block_stop`, and keep a heartbeat timeout longer than the pauses

pitfalls.symptom: A background result is gone under ZDR
pitfalls.cause: Data stays on disk only for roughly 10 minutes for polling
pitfalls.fix: Poll early and write the result to your own store

pitfalls.symptom: Background plus streaming feels slow on Azure
pitfalls.cause: A known performance issue when the two combine
pitfalls.fix: Use background with polling, or stream without background

scenarios.title: A streaming chat that also calls tools
scenarios.situation: A chat UI streams text and the model sometimes calls a tool that sends an email. Users complain that the first token is slow, and an incident sent an email with a truncated address.
constraints: Streaming is wanted for first-token speed
scenarios.question: How do you design the stream handling?

options.name: Run the tool as soon as its arguments start to arrive, to save time
options.why: Partial arguments caused the incident. A tool must not run before the call item is complete.
options.tradeoff: Prefetching read-only data from partial hints can be safe when it has no side effects.

options.name: Stream text to the UI, buffer tool calls, validate arguments after the item is done, then execute with a confirmation for side effects
options.why: It keeps the fast first token and removes the partial-action risk.
options.tradeoff: A short delay before tools run and more state handling.

options.name: Turn streaming off whenever tools are enabled
options.tradeoff: Users lose the early tokens, so perceived latency rises.

flips.then: You can start fetching earlier, still validating before use.
Skip streaming and take the final object.

scenarios.takeaway: Stream for humans, act on completed items only.

scenarios.title: A 20 minute research run behind a 60 second gateway
scenarios.situation: A web app runs a deep research call that takes about 20 minutes. The load balancer cuts connections at 60 seconds. The company is under zero data retention.
constraints: A user wants the result in the same session
unknowns: Can the UI show progress through polling?
scenarios.question: What do you build?

options.name: Hold one streaming connection open for 20 minutes
options.why: The gateway cuts it at 60 seconds, so the run is lost or must restart.
options.tradeoff: Long streams work only when no intermediary enforces a short timeout.

options.name: Submit through Batch and notify later
options.tradeoff: Up to 24 hours is too slow for a user waiting in session.

options.name: Use `background: true`, poll for status with a progress UI, and persist the result to your own store within the retention window
options.why: It survives the timeout, and storing the result yourself respects ZDR's short polling window.
options.tradeoff: You build polling, error handling and a result store.

flips.if: The user can come back tomorrow
No ZDR and results may live with the provider
flips.then: Keep `store=true` and poll the stored response.

scenarios.takeaway: Timeouts push long work to background and polling.

scenarios.title: Two million documents overnight
scenarios.situation: A nightly job classifies two million short documents. Results are needed by morning.
unknowns: Does the policy allow Batch for this data?
Is the 50,000 request limit per file acceptable?
scenarios.question: Which delivery mode do you use?

options.name: Batch API, split into files within the request and size limits
options.why: It gives a 50% discount, a separate rate-limit pool and a 24 hour window that fits the morning deadline [[r37]].
options.tradeoff: No interactive feedback, and OpenAI batches are not ZDR eligible.

options.name: Background mode for each document
options.why: It targets long single calls, and two million polls add load without a discount.
options.tradeoff: Background fits a few long calls that exceed a timeout.

options.name: Synchronous calls with high concurrency
options.tradeoff: Standard price, rate-limit pressure and retry handling.

flips.then: Batch is not eligible, so use synchronous calls with careful rate limiting.
Use synchronous calls or a priority tier.

quiz.q: Order these OpenAI Responses stream events.
quiz.explain: A response is created, an item is added, text deltas arrive, the text completes and then the response completes.

quiz.q: A Claude stream pauses for several seconds while a tool call is being generated. What is the likely cause?
options: Tool input arrives one complete key and value at a time
quiz.explain: Anthropic streams tool input one complete key and value at a time, so pauses are normal. A `ping` event may also appear in any position.

quiz.q: Which practices make streaming with tools safe?
options: Run side-effect tools only after the item is complete and validated
Execute tools from partial arguments to cut latency
Buffer deltas until a block ends
Confirm risky actions with the user
quiz.explain: Complete items, buffering and confirmation prevent partial-action incidents. Executing from partial arguments is the cause of them.

flashcards.front: How long does ZDR background data stay on disk for polling?
flashcards.back: Roughly 10 minutes. Poll promptly and persist the result yourself.

flashcards.front: Which Anthropic events carry tool input deltas?
flashcards.back: `content_block_delta` with `input_json_delta`, arriving one complete key and value at a time.

flashcards.front: Which mode do you pick when nobody is waiting?
flashcards.back: Batch: 50% of Standard, a 24 hour window and a separate rate-limit pool.
